html:
The Second Punic War was fought from 218 to 201 BCE between Rome and Carthage. It began with Hannibal invading Italy and ended with Rome as the strongest power in the western Mediterranean.

  • 218 BCE: Hannibal crosses the Alps and beats the Romans at the Trebia.
  • 217 BCE: He destroys a Roman army at Lake Trasimene. Rome turns to Fabius Maximus, who avoids battle.
  • 216 BCE: At Cannae Hannibal surrounds and wipes out a huge Roman army. Much of southern Italy goes over to him, and Macedon allies with Carthage.
  • 211 BCE: Rome retakes Capua; Syracuse falls after a siege made famous by the machines of Archimedes.
  • 209 to 206 BCE: Scipio drives Carthage out of Spain. Hannibal's brother Hasdrubal reaches Italy with a second army but is killed at the Metaurus in 207 BCE.
  • 202 BCE: Scipio invades Africa and beats Hannibal at the Battle of Zama.

Rome won because it would not give in and could raise army after army from its Italian allies. Carthage gave up Spain and its fleet and paid a huge indemnity. Our main sources are Polybius and Livy.
